title: Gold Ark — Sira chronology
status: Dates as stated in the quoted sources; differing views side by side
rules: Dates only as quoted; nothing converted or estimated
Sunni and Shia views side by side, no ranking
Ibn Sa'd month count: 'at the head of N months from his Hijra' -> month N counted with Rabi al-Awwal 1 AH as month 1; year shown only when the month he names matches.
Day idioms ('when six nights had passed', 'when five remained') -> day not shown; wording kept in the quote.
Estimated values are labelled as estimated, with the source quoted.

entries.notes: The Monday opinion gives only the weekday, no day or month. WikiShia also says 'Some Shi'a scholars have considered the twelfth of Rabi' I as the date', and that the 12 Rabi I date 'is the basis for practices in Mecca and Medina'. Wikipedia Mawlid adds that 'others contend that the date of Muhammad's birth is unknown'. Wikipedia Year of the Elephant gives the year as 'approximately equating to 570–571 CE' and says 'Some others have placed the Year of the Elephant one or two decades earlier than 570 CE'. The 570 CE in the WikiShia quote dates the destruction of Abraha's army; WikiShia (al-Jahiz) ties the birth to the same year. No Gregorian day given by any source; none computed.

Wikipedia also: 'Hans Wehr says that the 27th night of the month of Rajab chosen for the Miraj is not based on a report and is an arbitrary choice'. Ibn Sa'd (via Wikipedia) treats Mi'raj (27 Ramadan) and Isra (17 Rabi al-Awwal) as separate events; Wikipedia gives '27th' for Ramadan (checked twice) — other works often cite Ibn Sa'd for 17 Ramadan, so this should be checked against Ibn Sa'd directly. The al-islam.org lecture attributes the 'within days' view to Ibn Sa'd and adds that 'Other historians state it happened several months after, possibly five months or more after.' WikiShia also describes an earlier brotherhood pact among Muhajirun in Mecca before the Hijra and a later one in 9 AH; those are separate events and not recorded here. Wikipedia gives no date. No sunnah.com hadith with a date was found. [Note: year added from WikiShia 'Pact of Brotherhood between Muhajirun and Ansar' (first year of Hijra/622; al-Mufid 12 Ramadan 1 AH). Other reports: 3, 5 or 8 months after the Hijra, or within days — so the circle shows the year only.]

entries.notes: Strong conflicts. Gregorian: WikiShia March 4–24, 627; Wikipedia infobox 31 March – c. 14 April 627; Wikipedia siege section 'began in January 627' (internal contradiction on the same page; the same page also says the Confederate army marched 'In December 626'). Hijri: WikiShia says 5 AH by 'the majority of historians' (its own wording), with Shawwal or Dhu al-Qa'da for the month; Wikipedia gives 5 Shawwal–1 Dhu al-Qi'dah with no year in that sentence. WikiShia's range sentence gives weekdays for start (Thursday) and end (Saturday); weekday field left empty because there are two. Durations vary: 'around two weeks', 'two or three weeks', '20 nights', '27 days'. sunnah.com Sahih al-Bukhari 4104 (chapter 'The Ghazwa of Al-Khandaq or Al-Ahzab Battle') was fetched: its English page states no date.
entries.placement: Gold Ark (AI): FLAGGED DATED ENTRY. The Trench (Shawwal-Dhu al-Qa'da 5 AH) must precede the siege of Qurayza (GL-C-15) and al-Qurata' (Muharram 6 AH); currently it comes after both. Its 27 sub-events follow it.

entries.notes: The letters were sent at different times, so there is no single date. The WikiShia lead also says: "the majority of accounts place them in the sixth year after the Hijra, following the Treaty of Ḥudaybiyya" (wording of the source, not ours). Wikipedia gives no overall date; its only dated item is the Oman letter (628 AD, the date of the rulers' acceptance, not of sending). Wikipedia says of the letter to the Negus that it is not known whether it went with Ja'far on the migration to Abyssinia "or at a later date following the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah". islamqa answer 36861 was checked and states no date.

opinions.label: Ibn Kathir: the dawn prayer of Monday, the day of death

hijri.text: صلاة الصبح من يوم الاثنين يوم الوفاة

sources.label: Ibn Kathir, al-Bidaya wa al-Nihaya, vol 8 p.54
sources.section: [ذكر أمره عليه الصلاة والسلام أبا بكر الصديق رضي الله عنه أن يصلي بالصحابة أجمعين] مع حضورهم كلهم وخروجه، عليه الصلاة والسلام، فصلى وراءه مقتديا به في بعض الصلوات على ما سنذكره، وإماما له ولمن بعده من الصحابة
sources.quote: قال البيهقي: ففي هذا دلالة أن هذه الصلاة كانت صلاة الصبح من يوم الاثنين يوم الوفاة ;
sources.quote_en: Al-Bayhaqi said: in this is an indication that this prayer was the dawn prayer of Monday, the day of death;

hijri.text: لم يصل يوم الاثنين صلاة الصبح مع الناس، وأنه كان قد انقطع عنهم ; لم يخرج إليهم ثلاثا

sources.label: Ibn Kathir, al-Bidaya wa al-Nihaya, vol 8 p.55
sources.section: [ذكر أمره عليه الصلاة والسلام أبا بكر الصديق رضي الله عنه أن يصلي بالصحابة أجمعين] مع حضورهم كلهم وخروجه، عليه الصلاة والسلام، فصلى وراءه مقتديا به في بعض الصلوات على ما سنذكره، وإماما له ولمن بعده من الصحابة
sources.quote: فهذا أوضح دليل على أنه، عليه الصلاة والسلام، لم يصل يوم الاثنين صلاة الصبح مع الناس، وأنه كان قد انقطع عنهم ; لم يخرج إليهم ثلاثا
sources.quote_en: This is the clearest proof that he did not pray the dawn prayer of Monday with the people, and that he had been cut off from them; he did not come out to them for three days.

opinions.label: Ibn Sa'd: Thursday

sources.label: Ibn Sa'd, al-Tabaqat al-Kubra, vol 2 p.186
sources.section: ذكر الكتاب الذي أراد رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - أن يكتبه لأمته في مرضه الذي مات فيه
sources.quote: اشتكى النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - يوم الخميس فجعل. يعني ابن عباس. يبكي ويقول يوم الخميس وما يوم الخميس! اشتد بالنبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - وجعه فقال: ائتوني بدواة وصحيفة

sources.section: ذكر الكتاب الذي أراد رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - أن يكتبه لأمته في مرضه الذي مات فيه

opinions.label: Ibn Sa'd: Thursday

sources.quote: كان يقول يوم الخميس وما يوم الخميس! قال: وكأني أنظر إلى دموع ابن عباس على خده كأنها نظام اللؤلؤ! قال قال رسول الله. ص: ائتوني بالكتف والدواة

entries.notes: Opinions recorded side by side; no ranking. Wording such as 'most well-known', 'majority', 'not correct' is the sources' own and appears only inside quotes. Age opinions and weekday-only opinions have no calendar date, so all date fields are null and precision is 'traditional'. Wikipedia's 'aged 61–62' (infobox, inside the 8 June 632 quote) is a further age figure. WikiShia notes the Shia historian Rasul Ja'farian says no narration directly supports 28 Safar. Gregorian equivalents differ by source (May 25 for 28 Safar; June 7 per WikiShia and June 8 per Wikipedia for the Sunni date); not reconciled. al-islam.org page also contains the line 'In the 10th year of Hijrat, he passed away on 28th Safar' (year as written there; not used). Year 11 AH: islamqa says 'there is no difference of opinion' that it was 11 AH; WikiShia lead says '11 AH/632 CE'. Same source URL appears in more than one opinion here (different quote each) because one page lists several opinions.
